newsitem.title: NORWAY: "Millennium bug" may cost Norway 30 bln NOK-report.
newsitem.headline: "Millennium bug" may cost Norway 30 bln NOK-report.

text.p: Solving the "Millennium bug" will cost Norwegian companies and the public sector an estimated 30 billion crowns ($4.2 billion), financial daily Dagens Naeringsliv said on Monday.
It quoted a study by Norsk Brukergruppe, a millennium-bug association formed by Norwegian companies.

The Millennium bug is a world-wide programming problem that will cause many computers to view the year 2000 as the year 1900. The bug will occur as a result of a programming fault which only allows computers to accept the last two digits of a year.
As a result, companies will have to re-programme their computers to accept a four-digit field before 2000 in order to avoid computer chaos.

"A big Norwegian company will have to spend between 50 and 100 million crowns to make sure that its computers function in the year 2000," according to the report, which was based on international studies of the software problem.
Norwegian companies will have to spend around 18 billion crown and the public sector 12 billion to overcome the problem, Dagens Naeringsliv said.
